subject.title: feat(ios): Siri App Intent integration — native "Hey Siri, ask OpenClaw..." support

question: Should first-party iOS Siri/AppIntent execution be added, and should it route through paired node.event agent.request, operator chat.send, or a hardened hooks boundary with explicit confirmation and spoken-reply policy?
rationale: The codebase has adjacent chat, Talk, share, deep-link, and hook primitives, but choosing one for Siri affects auth, session state, confirmation, and user-visible security posture.

options.title: Approve Design-Gated Native Intent
options.body: Implement Siri/AppIntent support only after maintainers choose the auth boundary, session semantics, confirmation policy, and spoken-reply behavior, then require real iOS device proof.

options.title: Limit To Talk Mode Launch
options.body: Treat first-party Shortcuts support as launching the app or Talk Mode only, leaving parameterized Siri questions out of scope for now.

options.title: Keep Webhook Workaround External
options.body: Decline first-party Siri agent execution until demand or extension APIs justify the security surface, leaving Shortcuts plus webhook as the workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve Design-Gated Native Intent
recommendation.body: Implement Siri/AppIntent support only after maintainers choose the auth boundary, session semantics, confirmation policy, and spoken-reply behavior, then require real iOS device proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-main signal for iOS product direction and adjacent native app platform work.
